nodes.description: HERC1 is a TSC2-interacting ubiquitin ligase; TSC1 stabilizes TSC2 by excluding HERC1 from the complex, and HERC1-TSC2 interaction destabilizes and degrades TSC2, the GTPase-activating protein that restrains mTORC1. In the gain-of-function family, mTORC1 activity stays high and S6K1 remains phosphorylated in patient fibroblasts under starvation. Megalencephaly and somatic overgrowth are the clinical signatures of excess mTOR-pathway growth signaling; the failure of starvation-induced autophagy measured in the same cells is modeled as a separate downstream node.
